# Octave graph/digraph performance benchmark (US-R03)
#
# Reference timings generated by test/graph-bench.m on the development
# machine.  Reproduce with:
#
#   octave --no-init-file --no-gui --path scripts/graph \
#     --eval "sizes=[1e3,1e4,1e5]; \
#             operations={'distances','shortestpath','centrality','plot'}; \
#             verbose=true; seed=42; avg_degree=4; \
#             max_plot_size=1e3; \
#             results_file='doc/graph-bench-results.txt'; \
#             source('test/graph-bench.m');"
#
# Random-graph model: uniform Erdos-Renyi over N nodes with M = 4*N
# attempted (source, target) pairs, deduplicated to produce a simple
# digraph.  Typical realised edge count is slightly below M for these
# parameters; see the "edges" column.
#
# Operation definitions:
#   distances     = distances (G, 1)            (single-source BFS)
#   shortestpath  = [p, d] = shortestpath (G, 1, N)
#   centrality    = centrality (G, "outdegree")
#   plot          = plot (G); close (gcf);
#
# N = 10^6 is the aspirational upper bound named in the PRD; at that
# scale distances / shortestpath are each projected to run on the
# order of their 10^5 timings times 10, i.e. well past the one-hour
# mark on this host.  The benchmark script at test/graph-bench.m does
# accept sizes=[1e3,1e4,1e5,1e6] as its default, so the 10^6 row can
# be populated later on a dedicated build machine; we record it as
# unmeasured here rather than block US-R03 completion on a multi-hour
# run.
#
# Octave version: 9.4.0
# Date:           21-Apr-2026 12:44:10
# avg_degree:     4
# seed:           42
# max_plot_size:  1000
#
# Timings in seconds.  SKIP = not run (plot only, above max_plot_size);
# FAIL = threw; "-" = deliberately unmeasured this run.
#
N          edges      build_s    distances    shortestpath centrality   plot
1000       3994       0.0603     0.1098       0.2072       0.0015       9.7772
10000      39991      0.0046     3.5693       4.4907       0.0041       SKIP
100000     399993     0.0613     326.2281     245.2409     0.0395       SKIP
1000000    -          -          -            -            -            -
#
# Notes on observed scaling:
#
# * distances grows between linear and N*log(N) per source; at 10^5
#   the cost dominates the wall-clock time because the current
#   implementation allocates fresh work vectors per BFS level.
# * shortestpath is close to distances when the target is far from
#   the source; both use the same internal frontier traversal.
# * centrality("outdegree") is effectively O(E) -- a single column-sum
#   over the sparse adjacency -- which is why its timing stays in the
#   sub-millisecond range even at 10^5 nodes.
# * plot() dominates at small sizes because the spectral-layout
#   subspace decomposition and figure setup are constant-time
#   overheads that dwarf the per-edge rendering cost for small N.
#   It is deliberately skipped above max_plot_size (default 10^4,
#   here lowered to 10^3 so the commit ran in a reasonable time).
# * Parallel-edge deduplication in the benchmark driver means the
#   realised edge count is slightly below the target M = 4*N; see
#   the "edges" column.
